Results.ReviewText:
I have to start the story here because you need context.
I had already spent my Birthday and Father's Day gifts earlier in the year on tools but the Sunday before my Birthday my wife asked "Have you ever considered an electric pellet gill/smoker?"  I said "I've thought about it but they are expensive." She then said "Well, Traeger's are on sale so I was thinking if you want one for your Birthday/Father's Day gift you can get one."  So I started researching Traegers and though the Eastwood 22 was $100 cheaper I settled on the Pro Series 22 for the simple facts that it has 2 integrated meat probes and a larger cook surface.  So I called Home Depot and asked how much it was to deliver and that was a mistake!!! I then looked on Traeger's website for dealers and found one in my town.  I went down and saw that they had the Pro Series 575 on display and knew that the wife wouldn't let me drop that much $$$ so I asked if they could order me a Pro Series 22.  They checked to see if they could and found that they actually had 2 in stock.  This was the best purchase I have ever made in the grillin'/smokin' world!!!  In the  3 weeks I've owned it I've made the best Baby Backs of my life, I've made the best pulled pork my wife's entire family has ever had.  Yes, each one of them came up to me and said it was the best they've ever had!!  I've also cremated a store bought pizza because 1, it was store bought and 2, I didn't have a stone and just tried to make it on the rack.  The toppings were perfect but the crust was a solid black throughout.  I'm going to try and make homemade pizza tomorrow with the leftover pulled pork we have.  My only complaint is the price of meat right now!!!
I can't say enough about this grill!!!  Rock Solid construction.  Top Notch technology to make it easy to grill/smoke like a pro.  The best part is that there is no foul odors or tastes from propane or charcoal starter fluid.  I would highly recommend this product to anyone and everyone that likes grilled/smoked foods!!!!

Results.ReviewText:
Purchased a "Mesa 22" model from Costco - near as I can tell, it's the same as the Pro 22 minus the upper rack.

I'm about 6 cooks in to it, and so far, mostly so good. Ribs came out good (only reason they weren't great is my technique was off), spatchcock chicken was incredible, hot smoked salmon was awesome... and then there was the Pork Butt.

I tucked the butt in at 6pm, anticipating an overnight cook. Used a blend of two different Traeger pellets (Hickory & Cherry) from two freshly opened bags. Smoker ran for a few hours, then gave me the LER error which I discovered around 11pm. I got it fired back up, watched it until about 1:30am - it seemed stable. Went to bed, up at 6am - LER error again, and a hunk of 70º meat. Vacuumed everything out of the firebox, started it up again, and it ran until about 2pm - and it happened a third time. Ended up finishing the butt in our oven.

I read that an incorrect starting procedure can cause this, so I will be meticulously following that this coming weekend when I try another one. Also seems possible that the pellets aren't in great shape (but they look fine - shiny & not crumbly at all - the bags were brand new). If that's the case, it'll be irritating to have spent $40 on bad fuel.

The cooks that have finished properly have been fantastic, and I'm not ready to rule out user error with the Butt fiasco, however I have to admit being a bit skeptical about trusting the grill to handle its business unattended. It'll have to work nicely for quite a while for me to trust it for another overnight session.

Results.ReviewText: My Traeger Pro 34 Pellet Grill air temps have consistently ran ~20-30 degrees below the Control Dial Set Temperature since I started using it last year.  The read out on the Traeger Control reads 20-30 degrees above the actual air temperature of the grill.  If I want the grill to run slightly below 225 degrees I have to set the Control to 250 degrees.  If I want the grill to run near 250 degrees I have to set the Control to 275 degrees.  The attached pictures were taken last year showing the difference between what the Traeger Control read out and the Thermoworks Smoke and Chef Thermometers using air probes.  The attached graphs from this year shows the variation between set point and actual grill air temp.  I use Traeger Pellets that are stored inside.  I sent two e-mails to the address in my Traeger Owner’s Manual, no response.  I sent message via Facebook asking for a working e-mail, nothing supplied, just said call 1-800 number.  Did that today, asked for a call back since the wait time was 55 minutes, 5 hours later still no call back.  All the bad Customer Service reports are true.  I bought a Pro 34 in 8/2018, started using it in 2019.
Results.Title: Ok Grill - Poor Customer Service

Results.ReviewText: I love the grill. In fact, I used it 10 straight days once it arrived. I cooked everything from steak, pulled pork, and smoked salmon. The Pro 34 doesn't have all the bells and whistles that the new models have, but it does have the same ease of use. The grill heats easily and maintains temperature +/- 5 degrees. Smoke comes easily and the app has awesome recipes. My only complaint is about searing meat. It's all but impossible without added grill grates. With that said, you're going to have that issue with any pellet grill.  I'd give it 4.5 stars if I could, but I always round down when it's not an option. The Pro 34 is a fantastic value and a welcome addition to my outdoor cooking area.
